blocks.text: How Does Red Light Therapy Work and Why is it Popular in Biohacking

Infrared light therapy is far from new in physical therapy treatments. NASA first used infrared lamps in the 70s to rehabilitate astronauts, scientists, and military personnel after challenging missions and tests. For a long time, infrared therapy was a privilege for wealthy people. However, infrared lamps appeared in ordinary medical centers in the United States and Europe over time. The high efficiency of red and infrared light physiotherapy brought the procedure into trend, attracted the attention of celebrities, and made the procedure available to each of us.

Red Light Therapy is a therapeutic effect on the body using a powerful stream of natural red and infrared light with a length of 650-850 nm. RLT technology is based on the natural ability of cell mitochondria to absorb light and convert it into energy. Light therapy causes several biochemical reactions in cells: it accelerates tissue regeneration, stops inflammatory processes, and stimulates elastin and collagen production.

Over the last few decades, research about RLT therapy has appeared in reputable scientific publications. It has been scientifically proven that red and near-infrared light stimulates the mitochondria to produce extracellular energy through AFT acid. Extracellular energy is necessary to recover quickly, fight viral and infectious diseases, and fight oxidative stress. By enhancing ATP production, the infrared lamp fights free radicals and promotes the production of natural human antioxidants.

After an RLT treatment, you will always feel energized. At the same time, your inner state will be relaxed and calm. Japanese and American scientists have proven that infrared therapy neutralizes stress’s effects, normalizes man’s circadian biorhythms, and adjusts sleep. The fact is that artificial blue light from smartphones and computers negatively affects human biorhythms and leads to chronic insomnia. Red light has the opposite effect because it has a temperature as close as possible to natural light.

Red and infrared light therapy calms the central nervous system, relaxes, and prepares a person for sleep. In his book Game Changers, the world’s foremost biohacker, Dave Asprey, recommends using infrared lamps daily for healthy sleep.
What is the Difference Between Infrared and Red Light

Infrared light is invisible electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength of 850 nm or more. Infrared rays do not heat the air. However, they can penetrate our body up to 8-10 mm to the cellular level, triggering regenerative processes there. Infrared light therapy is used for therapeutic and medical purposes.

Red light has wavelengths in the range of 600 to 850 nm. Reaching fibroblasts responsible for the synthesis of elastin and collagen, red light activates their production. It promotes the natural regeneration of the skin. Red light therapy is most commonly used for cosmetic procedures.
Red Light Therapy Devices

Both LED and laser devices – beds, lamps, helmets, and face masks – are readily available in clinical and non-clinical settings. They are used in medical spas, gyms, and beauty salons. Gadgets can be purchased for the home as well.

Laser devices are more powerful and are commonly used by hospitals. LEDs are less powerful and are more commonly used in commercial or home settings. The consensus is that LEDs can be used in beauty salons as long as the technicians are properly trained.
Red Light Therapy Mask

LED mask is a high-tech device with LEDs of different wavelengths used by cosmetologists in multi-stage skin care. The device’s principle of operation is based on the skin’s ability to absorb light rays and convert them into energy.

The technology used in the LED mask was developed by NASA and has been used in medicine for more than 40 years. The device has different effects on the skin. It all depends on the color chosen by the user at a particular moment. Light waves have different wavelengths, meaning they penetrate deeper or act superficially. For example, red has a wavelength of 620-750 nm, while blue has a 476-495 nm wavelength.

Benefits of Biohacking With Red Light Therapy
Skin Health and Anti-Aging

Red light stimulates the body’s cells, energizing them, activating blood flow to the affected area, and stimulating healing. The treatment is simple and painless: during the treatment, the patient sits comfortably or lies down for three to fifteen minutes without discomfort or pain. There may be a sensation of warmth, but it should not be unpleasant or hot. The use of protective eyewear is also recommended.

When used properly, red light therapy is safe, but Praveen Arani, professor of oral biology and biomedical engineering at the University of Buffalo, cautions against overdosing. The expert refers to staying under the light for too long or treatments with too much power. This doesn’t necessarily cause harm but can reduce or delay the effects. That said, just as some people are more prone to sunburn, some patients may be more sensitive to light. In such cases, lower doses of light are recommended.
In addition, the infrared lamp has a powerful cosmetic effect:

items: Stimulates the production of elastin and collagen.
Increases skin firmness and elasticity.

Pain Relief

In case of muscle pain or cramps, heat radiation helps muscle tissues to relax; due to intensive blood flow, they start to be actively supplied with nutrients and oxygen. The pain passes, and the spasming muscles relax. The procedure duration depends on the degree of pain, usually 15-20 minutes. In sciatica, pain in the shoulder and lumbar region – the distance of the device from the painful area of the body is 20-25 cm. The irradiated area does not necessarily need to be exposed. To prevent burns, it is better to heat through a cotton cloth. Arthritis, arthrosis, and other diseases that cause joint pain are some of the main indications for using infrared lamps. Created under IR rays, intense blood flow, and leukocytes coming to the tissues help reduce inflammation and remove toxins. The procedure is carried out for 20-30 minutes.
Hair Growth

Red light therapy, also known as low-intensity laser therapy (LILT), is a non-invasive treatment that uses red or near-infrared light to [stimulate hair growth](http://biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-secrets-for-hair). This therapy involves exposing the scalp to light emitted from laser devices.
Is Red Light Therapy Safe?

Yes, red light therapy (RLT) is generally considered safe when used correctly. It is non-invasive, does not emit UV radiation, and has minimal side effects. Most studies suggest that RLT can benefit skin health, wound healing, pain relief, and muscle recovery. However, some precautions include:

items: **Eye Protection:** Avoid direct exposure to the eyes, as intense light can be harmful.
**Skin Sensitivity:** Some people may experience mild redness or irritation.
**Proper Usage:** Overuse or incorrect application may reduce effectiveness or cause discomfort.

blocks.text: If you have any underlying conditions, it’s best to consult a healthcare professional before starting red light therapy.
Expert Thoughts on Biohacking With Red Light Therapy

Praveen Arani, Professor of Oral Biology and Biomedical Engineering at the University at Buffalo, discussed red light therapy. As an expert in the use of light and laser for medical purposes, he explained how everything works and which diseases the technique can be useful for. Most importantly, Arani explained whether the home devices, which anyone can buy, are effective.

“Light therapy involves exposure to red light in very low doses in a hospital or clinic. It is also referred to as low-power laser therapy, soft laser therapy, cold laser therapy, and non-thermal LED light therapy.”

All of these are described by the general term “photobiomodulation therapy,” which involves using other colors or wavelengths spanning the visible and near-infrared spectrum for health. Arani notes that red light has recently become popular due to its availability. However, it has been used for more than thirty years.

Arani says red light therapy can reduce pain, inflammation, and tissue damage. Since these are common in many conditions, photobiomodulation can be a powerful adjunct for treating many conditions. One example is cancer and the use of the technique to reduce pain and inflammation from radiation, chemotherapy, and bone marrow stem cell transplants. The expert also notes that clinical studies show the effectiveness of photobiomodulation in healing diabetic and burn wounds, as well as certain types of ulcers.

Dave Asprey, one of the pioneers of biohacking, is a big proponent of infrared therapy. He claims that red light can improve overall health, speed the body’s recovery, and maintain optimal cellular health. The main benefits of infrared therapy, according to Asprey, are:

items: Detoxification – infrared heat promotes deep sweating, removing toxins from the body.
Improved circulation – infrared waves penetrate deeper into the tissues, dilating blood vessels and increasing blood circulation.
Restore and reduce inflammation – helps reduce inflammation and speeds up the healing of muscles and joints.
Mitochondrial support – infrared radiation stimulates ATP production, increasing cell energy exchange.
Relaxation and stress reduction – helps lower cortisol levels and improve sleep.

**Tracking Health Markers** : Monitoring health metrics provides insights into the effectiveness of biohacks. Utilizing red light therapy can positively influence these markers, offering measurable improvements.
